The *Soṇātherīapadāna* (Thi Ap 26) is a verse narrative located within the Therīapadāna section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The text belongs to the apadāna genre, recounting the past karmic aspirations and spiritual attainments of the elder nun (*therī*) Soṇā. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the work across five languages [SuttaCentral].
While direct narrative parallels across Buddhist traditions are not curated on SuttaCentral, related textual material connects this text to Dhammapada verse 112 (Dhp 112) and its cognate versions in the "Thousand" chapters across various traditions [SuttaCentral]. These include the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (G-Dhp 305–321 Sahasravagga), the Patna Dharmapada (P-Dhp 376–397 Sahasravagga), the Mahāvastu (San Lo Mvu 109), Chinese Dharmapada translations (T 210.16, T 212.25, and T 213.24), and Udānavarga transmissions in Sanskrit and Tibetan (UV 24, Uv Kg 24, UVS 24) [SuttaCentral].
Computational text-reuse data from DharmaNexus identifies 238 matching passages shared with 46 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial correspondence occurs with the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, which quotes or parallels almost the entire text (segments §0.3–22.1 aligned with §1450–1493) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, substantial formulaic verses are shared with other female and male apadānas, including the *Paṭācārātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 20), *Dhammadinnātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 23), *Siṅgālamātutherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 34), *Kisāgotamītherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 22), *Nandātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 25), and *Kāḷudāyittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 548) [DharmaNexus].
